clue.text: Roundabout island in Bury's also a feature of Leigh

parts.note: to bury something is to secrete it, so 'bury's' (buries) gives the verb form secretes, here clipped as written: secrets
also is a plain synonym of and

indicators.note: roundabout suggests going round in circles, so the word for island is turned about into a new order

parts.note: an isle is an island

explanation.surface: A traffic roundabout with a central island in the town of Bury is said to share something with the town of Leigh.
explanation.walkthrough: Bury and Leigh look like two Lancashire towns, but Leigh is the film director Mike Leigh. 'Roundabout' rearranges ISLE to LIES; 'in' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1996 film by director Mike Leigh, a feature film being one he made.

clue.text: Professor and tramp selling poultry in street?

parts.note: to tramp is to walk heavily, to step
a hen is a poultry bird
hawking is selling goods by calling in the street, which 'in street?' hints at

explanation.surface: A tramp is pictured peddling chickens on a street corner, with a professor somehow involved.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'selling poultry in street' as hens being hawked, then put the pieces in answer order after STEP; 'in street?' just colours the hawking.
explanation.definitionFit: The Cambridge physicist held the Lucasian chair of mathematics, a famous professorship.

clue.text: Bags of this? X amount

parts.note: X is the Greek letter chi
No is the abbreviation for number, an amount

explanation.surface: A puzzle asking how much of some material makes up a pair of trousers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bags' is old British slang for loose trousers; trousers made of this cotton twill take its name.
explanation.definitionFit: Chino is a twill cotton cloth, from which casual trousers (bags) are cut.

clue.text: Urge, etc, people to hold piano competition

parts.note: to egg on is to urge

indicators.note: to hold means the words for etc and people take the piano letter inside them

parts.note: etc is short for et cetera, which means and so on
p is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly
a race is a people

explanation.surface: Someone urges a group of people to put on a piano competition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to hold' puts P inside AND SO ON, between S and O, making AND SPOON, followed by RACE.
explanation.definitionFit: A school sports-day race in which runners balance an egg on a spoon, a contest.

clue.text: Country lawyer sporting shiner

indicators.note: sporting, as wearing, sets one piece within the other so the lawyer sits inside the shiner

parts.note: the sun is something that shines, a shiner
DA is a District Attorney, an American lawyer

explanation.surface: A rural lawyer turns up with a black eye.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shiner' wants to be a black eye; here it is the sun.
explanation.definitionFit: Sudan is a nation in north-east Africa.

clue.text: Honeymoon couple have day in Cornish town, finally partner-swapping

indicators.note: in places the day inside the altered name of the Cornish town
in bridge North and South are partners, so the final N is swapped for its partner S

parts.note: Newlyn is a fishing town in Cornwall
Wed is short for Wednesday, a day

explanation.surface: A newly married pair spend a day in a Cornwall resort and end up swapping spouses.
explanation.walkthrough: NEWLYN loses its last N to S, its bridge partner, giving NEWLYS; WED then goes in before the S.
explanation.definitionFit: People just married, on their wedding trip, are the recently wed.

clue.text: Send packing case with sides splitting?

definitions.meaning: a legal case where everyone is splitting their sides with mirth, so the court dissolves in laughter

explanation.surface: Dismissing a suitcase whose sides have burst.
explanation.definitionFit: To dismiss scornfully, and literally a court case collapsing in hilarity.

clue.text: One leading antelope without herd, unexpectedly

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the antelope surrounds the rest

parts.note: the eland is a large African antelope

indicators.note: unexpectedly shows the letters of herd come out in a surprising order

explanation.surface: A lone antelope leading the way without its herd, to everyone's surprise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' means outside: ELAND goes round DERH, the anagram of HERD from 'unexpectedly'.
explanation.definitionFit: In card games the elder hand is the player who leads first.

clue.text: Greet, in Cantonese, railway worker leaving? Yes, dismissed

indicators.note: in places the railway letters inside what remains of Cantonese
the worker leaving means those letters are taken out of Cantonese

parts.note: an ant is the classic crossword worker
a batsman dismissed in cricket is out

explanation.surface: Greeting someone in Cantonese while a railway worker quits and is sacked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Greet' is Scots for weep. Removing ANT from CANTONESE leaves CONESE; RY goes in after the C.
explanation.definitionFit: To greet in Scots is to weep, and weeping bitterly is the idiom.

clue.text: Exotic kirsch is neat — gets heads spinning?

indicators.note: the heads of the five words are their first letters

explanation.surface: Neat exotic kirsch makes drinkers' heads spin.
explanation.definitionFit: Spinning out a supply and eking it out both mean making it last longer.

clue.text: Flipping, flaming sister with overdraft in Oz

indicators.note: flipping turns the whole string over, so it is read from the end

parts.note: flaming red is the colour of fire
a nun is a religious sister
O/D is the bank abbreviation for overdrawn or overdraft

explanation.surface: A furious sister with debts at the bank, in Australia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flipping' and 'flaming' look like mild oaths; one reverses REDNUNWOD.
explanation.definitionFit: Australia is colloquially called the land down under.

clue.text: Social call from wise bird, the answer to Billy-no- Mates' prayers?

parts.note: the owl, the wise bird, gives a hoot

parts.words: the answer to Billy-no- Mates' prayers
parts.note: a billy goat with no mates would pray for a female goat, a nanny

explanation.surface: An owl calls out an invitation to a party, just what a friendless person wanted.
explanation.walkthrough: Billy-no-mates is British slang for a person without friends; here Billy is a billy goat.
explanation.definitionFit: An informal gathering with folk music and dancing, a social.

clue.text: Brother speechless when Labour a point short

indicators.note: short means the phrase is cut back by its last letter

parts.note: to labour a point is to harp on it

explanation.surface: A political sibling is lost for words when the Labour Party is one point down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Labour' looks like the party; it is the verb, as in labouring the point.
explanation.definitionFit: The Marx brother who never spoke on screen.

clue.text: Scratch back hard when meeting a girl

indicators.note: back means the word for Scratch is read in reverse

parts.note: Old Scratch is a nickname for the Devil, Satan
H is the pencil abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: Someone scratches another's back on meeting a girl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scratch' is the Devil (Old Scratch), not an itch.
explanation.definitionFit: A Russian female first name, as of Tolstoy's heroine Rostova.

clue.text: Song for which cha-chacha is more than necessary?

definitions.text: Song for which cha-chacha is more than necessary?

parts.words: Song for which cha-chacha is more than necessary?
parts.note: cha is slang for tea, so three chas would serve three people when the song title asks for only a pair

explanation.surface: A dance-band number for which a cha-cha-cha is overdoing it.
explanation.walkthrough: The cha-cha-cha is a dance, but cha is British slang for tea.
explanation.definitionFit: A 1925 show tune by Youmans and Caesar, a popular song.

clue.text: I can see no sense us messing with birds at boxing

indicators.note: messing with these words means jumbling their letters into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone sees no point in our fooling around with women at a boxing match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'messing' scrambles US, BIRDS and AT together; 'with' and 'boxing' are colour.
explanation.definitionFit: One who holds that life is meaningless says there is no sense in anything.

clue.text: Rival successfully departed, chasing bird

indicators.note: chasing means coming after, so the departed piece follows the bird

parts.note: the emu is a flightless Australian bird
the late are the departed

explanation.surface: A rival who has died is pursued by a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: To match or equal another, by imitation, is to rival them with success.

clue.text: In bafflement and fear, hiding arm in a sling

indicators.note: in puts the shortened fear inside the a-plus-sling pair

parts.note: to sling is to toss

indicators.note: hiding means the arm is put away, removed from the word for fear

parts.note: alarm is fear
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone baffled and frightened, with an injured arm in a sling.
explanation.walkthrough: ALARM hiding ARM leaves AL, which goes into A TOSS after the T.
explanation.definitionFit: Puzzled and unsure what to do is the idiomatic meaning.

clue.text: Foot deep snow, endless winds

indicators.note: winds, as in twists, means the letters are wound round into a new order
endless means the last letter of snow is cut off

explanation.surface: Deep snow and constant winds on a hike.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' trims SNOW to SNO; 'winds' then rearranges DEEP plus SNO. 'Foot' is a metrical foot.
explanation.definitionFit: A metrical foot of two long stressed syllables in verse.

clue.text: Going back a bit Jacklin won kudos in the Open

indicators.note: going back means the run of letters is read from right to left
a bit of means only part of these words is used, a run inside them

explanation.surface: A golfer recalls Tony Jacklin's glory at the Open Championship.
explanation.walkthrough: Tony Jacklin won the 1969 British Open golf championship; the Open here is simply public view.
explanation.definitionFit: What is out in the open is public, recognised by all.

clue.text: Cheaper cooking for one turning back heat

indicators.note: cooking the books means falsifying them, so the letters are doctored into a new order
turning back means the abbreviation for for one is read backwards

parts.note: eg, for example, means for one

explanation.surface: Budget cooking that involves turning the heat back down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooking' makes REPECHA from CHEAPER; 'turning back' gives GE. 'heat' is a sporting round, not warmth.
explanation.definitionFit: In rowing or cycling a repechage is an extra qualifying round, a heat for those who lost.

clue.text: What's seen in Paraguay is all too familiar

indicators.note: what is seen in something sits inside it, so all goes within the country code

parts.note: PY is the international code for Paraguay

explanation.surface: Something observed in Paraguay feels overly familiar.
explanation.definitionFit: Being chummy, over-friendly, is excessive familiarity.

clue.text: Poplar the first to be done in English capital

parts.words: the first to be done in
parts.note: Abel, killed by Cain, was the first person murdered in the Bible

indicators.note: a capital is the first letter of a word

explanation.surface: A poplar tree was the first thing felled in England's capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'done in' means killed; 'capital' takes the first letter of English.
explanation.definitionFit: The abele is the white poplar tree.

clue.text: Male in part thrawn, miserly, every other avoided

indicators.note: every other letter is skipped, keeping the second, fourth and so on

explanation.surface: A man described as partly stubborn and stingy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'thrawn' is Scots for stubborn. Start with N of 'in' and take alternate letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A man's given name, as of the American writer Hawthorne.
